root_idea.summary: The root centers on gathering or assembling something with weight, yielding the notions of burden, packing, preparation, and assigning importance.
root_idea.development: The evidence connects physical weight and packed arrangement with figurative evaluation: what has weight is regarded or valued, while what has no weight is disregarded. Related nominal developments include a load, an enclosing garment, and associated derived forms.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb, normalized from the imperfect Quranic form to the classical perfect citation form عَبَأَ.

senses.definition: To care about, heed, or regard as having weight or worth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence it appears in the negated construction مَا يَعْبَؤُا بِكُمْ رَبِّي, meaning not to care about or regard someone as having weight or importance; the construction may also be paraphrased as asking what would be done with them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pack goods or utensils; to put things together, prepare, set in order, or arrange them; to equip people for war, and to prepare evil or mischief for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of goods, utensils, supplies, horsemen, an army, or something prepared for another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, prepare, or mix perfume.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use with perfume as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To receive something with approbation or accept it favorably.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction عَبَأَ اللهُ عَنْهُ, distinct from the negative بِهِ or لَهُ construction expressing disregard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To think or opine something and adopt it as a tenet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with لِـ in عَبَأَ لَهُ, referring to holding something as an opinion or doctrine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shine or radiate, said of the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use alongside the unhamzated form عَبَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stuff the vulva with a مِعْبَأَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical and sexual use explicitly described in reference to a woman; the derived verb may occur without the instrumental phrase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put together for oneself, grasp, or gain possession of property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use of اعتبأ, presented with some qualification in the lexical evidence.
A reported nominal use with related variant forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A load, burden, or weight; especially a debt or other responsibility that one undertakes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of goods, debt, responsibility, or anything borne; the plural is أَعْبَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A half-load carried on one side of a beast and balanced by a corresponding load on the other side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized sense synonymous with عِدْلٌ; the plural is أَعْبَاءٌ.
Used in the expression هٰذَا عَبْءُ هٰذَا, meaning “this is the like of this.”
The supplied lexical evidence applies this adjective to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well-known woollen outer garment, a kind of كِسَاء, generally made with stripes; also described as a woollen جُبَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A garment term; عَبَايَةٌ is cited as a variant form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way of thinking adopted as a tenet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun equated with مَذْهَبٌ and connected in the evidence with عَبَأَ لَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The piece of rag used by a menstruating woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific article of menstrual hygiene; it is also the instrument named in the anatomical use of الاِعْتِبَاءُ.

cautions: The sole Quranic occurrence is 25:77; the displayed headword is normalized from the imperfect Quranic form to the Form I perfect citation form عَبَأَ.
The historical Quran citation notation in the lexical evidence is not converted into a modern verse location; 25:77 is used here because that location is independently supplied by QAC.
Distinct classical vocalizations and headwords such as عَبْءٌ, عِبْءٌ, عَبَاءٌ, and عَبَاءَةٌ are retained as separate lexical entries rather than being collapsed into the Quranic verb.
